diagnostic_evidence.quote: Regarding stability, the standard deviations reported for both methods are generally comparable in magnitude across the tested dimensions.
This aligns with the papers' claim that the DBR method produces more accurate estimations, particularly as the dimension increases.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims substantially reduced variance, better training stability and robustness up to d=20 with relative error under 9.7%. The tables do not show this. In Table 1 at d=200 DBR has a larger std (0.0071) than DBDP1 (0.0022). In Example 2, DBR's std is larger than DBDP1's in many rows (d=2, d=8, and d=20 at N=90,100). The text itself says the stds are 'comparable'. The 'Rel. err.' is computed from the 10-run sample mean, so it is a bias measure that hides run-to-run error. At d=20, N=90, DBR's mean absolute error is 0.366 against u=0.259 (about 141%), and it is larger than DBDP1's 0.265. The same holds at N=100. DBR's own std (0.446) exceeds the solution value. The claim that DBR improves 'particularly as the dimension increases' is contradicted by Table 1: DBR error rises from 1.44% at d=100 to 3.42% at d=200, while DBDP1 falls from 9.1% to 4.9%.

failure_location.quote: This architecture substantially mitigates numerical variance, resulting in enhanced training stability and superior generalization performance.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claims to what the tables support: lower error-of-the-mean in some high-dimensional settings, with comparable or larger run-to-run spread. Report per-run error metrics and drop or qualify the variance-reduction and dimension-trend claims.
issues.overall_effect: The headline numerical conclusions (variance mitigation, stability, d=20 robustness, growing advantage with dimension) are not supported by the data shown. The unqualified 'consistently outperforms' is also contradicted by the low-dimensional tables, where DBDP1 is often better.
issues.title: Variance-reduction and robustness claims contradicted by the reported tables
issues.why_classification: The headline empirical claims must be withdrawn or reformulated. The theory and the algorithm are unaffected, so a contained rewrite plus per-run metrics suffices.

issues.failure_explanation: The inner samples are generated only for time t_{i+1} (X_{i+1}^{\pi,m,k}). The Y-loss, however, evaluates f at X_i^{\pi,m,k} with Z at X_i^{\pi,m,k}. Those points are never generated, and they differ from the F_{t_i}-measurable point X_i^{\pi,m} required by the loss (DBR-loss-y) and the scheme. In addition, the backward loop i=N-1,...,0 uses X_i^{\pi,m} before the forward path has been simulated (X_i is regenerated inside the backward loop from an undefined predecessor). The next-step network is evaluated with theta^*_{y,i} instead of theta^*_{y,i+1}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Simulate the forward paths X_i^{\pi,m} once before the backward loop. Evaluate f and Z at (t_i, X_i^{\pi,m}), and use theta^*_{y,i+1} for the next-step network.
issues.overall_effect: The procedure as written is not a well-defined implementation of the DBR loss, so the reported numerical results cannot be tied to the stated scheme.
issues.title: Algorithm 1 uses undefined time-t_i quantities and evaluates f at the wrong point
issues.why_classification: A local rewrite of a few algorithm lines restores the intended loss and all claims.

issues.failure_explanation: The deviation of the label from its conditional expectation is bounded crudely by the full second moment of the network. This produces an additive constant C(1+h) in (Deep-NN-E-9-3-1) and an additive CN in (Deep-NN-E-9-z-1). The next displays, (Deep-NN-E-10) and (Deep-NN-E-16-1), silently drop these constants and keep only the R-terms. Retained, they contribute N·C per step to E|Y_i-U_i|^2/h and C to the Z-bound. After summation they give O(N^2) and O(N), which destroys the stated bound. In addition, E|Y_i-S_{y,i}|^2=E|R_{i,2}^y|^2 is asserted although R_{i,2}^y is defined with the exact quantities Y_{i+1}^{\pi,m,k}, Y_i^{\pi,m}, Z_i^{\pi,m}, whereas S_{y,i} is built from the networks. The needed estimate of S-U by the Monte-Carlo remainder R_{i,1} and the f-Lipschitz difference is never carried out.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo Steps 2 and 4: write S-U (and S_z-V) as the Monte-Carlo remainder plus an f-Lipschitz difference, bound those by the R_{i,1} terms and absorb the self-referential terms for small h. Fix the definition of R_{i,2} to match the training labels.
issues.overall_effect: The a posteriori error estimate, and hence the half-order convergence derived from it, is not established by the given proof. The RDBR theorem reuses 'the same arguments as in Step 2' and inherits the gap.
issues.title: Error bound proof drops O(1) terms: label variance bounded by second moments
issues.why_classification: The theorem's form and the later parameter choices survive, but the repair needs a new contained estimate for the label deviation and a consistent redefinition of the residuals.

issues.failure_explanation: To bound E[|A|^2 1_{|X|>R}] with E|A|^{2q} finite, Hölder gives (E|A|^{2q})^{1/q}·P(|X|>R)^{(q-1)/q}. The proof uses the conjugate exponent of 2q instead, giving P^{(2q-1)/q} and then an R^{-2} decay in terms of the lower norm ||X||_{2q/(2q-1)}. With X_0 only in L^{2+delta} and 2q=2+delta, the correct tail is only about R^{-delta}. The choice R=O(N^{3/2}) therefore does not give N^2(1+R^2eps^2)/R^2=O(1/N). The stated sizes kappa=O(N^3) and width O((2 sqrt(d) N^3)^{d^2-1}) are not justified under the stated hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: for $q>0$ and $2q = 2+\delta$ withe $\delta$ as in the statement of the proposition.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the Hölder/Markov step with the correct exponents. Assume enough moments of X_0 (e.g. deterministic x_0 as in Section 2, so Gaussian-driven moments are all finite) and recompute R, eps, kappa and the width accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed network sizes and the O(h) rate are unproved under the stated L^{2+delta} hypothesis on X_0. They would hold only with more moments (e.g. deterministic x_0) and different R, eps, kappa.
issues.title: Tail estimate in the convergence theorem uses incorrect Hölder exponents and unavailable moments
issues.why_classification: The rate survives under a strengthened moment assumption, but the stated parameter choices and the advertised L^{2+delta} scope change.

issues.failure_explanation: The reflected scheme requires the next-step value Y_{i+1}^\pi=max{ybar,g} inside the conditional expectations. The RDBR losses reuse S_{y,i} and S_{z,i} built from the raw network, and the auxiliary U-bar and V-hat are likewise defined with the raw network and no max with g. The output Y-hat_{i+1}=max{NN,g} is never fed back into the labels. The proof's recursion compares Y^\pi_{i+1} with the un-maxed network NN_{i+1}. The max-Lipschitz property gives control only of Y^\pi_{i+1}-Y-hat_{i+1}, not of Y^\pi_{i+1}-NN_{i+1}, which does not vanish where g exceeds the continuation value. No Gronwall closure of the recursion is given, and the final bound for max_i E|Y^\pi_i-Y-hat_i|^2 does not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the RDBR labels, U-bar and V-hat with Y-hat_{i+1}=max{NN_{i+1},g}. Then set up the one-step recursion in terms of Y^\pi_{i+1}-Y-hat_{i+1} and close it with a discrete Gronwall argument.
issues.overall_effect: The Y-error estimate for RDBR is unsupported. The scheme as defined does not discretize the RBSDE.
issues.title: RDBR labels omit the obstacle projection, so the scheme and proof do not match the reflected recursion
issues.why_classification: The scheme definition and the recursion argument must be redone, but the method, the form of the bound and the structure of the proof remain.

issues.failure_explanation: Steps 3-4 of Theorem 3.1 rely on the identity (FBSDE-err-z), obtained from the unreflected equation (FBSDE-t-i). The reflected equation has the extra term K_T-K_t, so that identity and the resulting bound on Z-bar minus V no longer hold as written. The theorem asserts the Z-error is bounded by C·epsilon(pi) with epsilon=O(h) under Assumption 2, but the cited discretization error for Z is only O(h^{1/2}) in both cases. The proof's final display (Deep-NN-E-8-R-11) also drops the epsilon(h) term obtained from the triangle inequality.

failure_location.quote: The error estimate for the $Z$-component can be derived using the same arguments as in Steps 3 and 4 of the proof of Theorem \ref{ae-DMCE}; thus, the details are omitted here.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the Z-error bound with the O(h^{1/2}) rate. Give an explicit Z-argument that accounts for the K-increment, and add the epsilon term to the Y-bound.
issues.overall_effect: The Z-part of the RDBR theorem is unproved. Under Assumption 2 its claimed O(h) order is inconsistent with the cited O(h^{1/2}) rate.
issues.title: RDBR Z-estimate omitted, not derivable as claimed, and the epsilon(pi) rate mismatches the cited Z-rate
issues.why_classification: A weaker Z-rate and a new argument for the reflection term are needed, but the Y-part and the overall structure remain.
